question: Can Google Pixel 4a users get through a normal day without recharging?
answer:
One reviewer states that with a 3140 mAh battery and a low-powered CPU, users will most probably get more than 1.5 days of operation time before recharging, assuming average screen time of around 2-2.5 hours per day. [994cdda37a2b_6]
A reviewer who uses the phone very frequently and charges it to 70 or 80% says they usually only have to charge it once a day. [e37282800dcd_1]
Another reviewer says they usually don't have to worry about running out of juice and often don't plug it in before going to sleep. [a9debe5022a9_2]
A reviewer of a renewed unit says battery life isn't great but sufficient. [aad680c1afc8_0]
One reviewer reports the battery does not last long and that it was dead after 3 hours of use. [6c54230ba402_0]
Another reviewer reports the phone running out of battery in a little more than 2 hours. [594806f0d0c9_0]

chunks.text: 4GB have been proven to not be enough for modern smartphones and thankfully Google packed 6GB in the 4a. That, combined with the 128GB of storage space, will allow users to download and install multiple apps without worrying about any shortcomings. Battery autonomy is great too. With 3140 milliamps per hour, and a low powered CPU, you will most probably get more than 1.5 days of operation time before you have to recharge (provided that the average screen time is around a modest 2-2.5 hours/day). The Google Pixel 4a is equipped with a 12 MP rear camera using the IMX363 sensor, with Optical & Electronic Image Stabilization (OIS + EIS). The aperture is f/1.7 and the field of view is 77 degrees. It can shoot 4K videos at 30fps or 1080p video at 60 fps.

RENEWED model : battery won't quick charge. This Pixel 4a has a lot going for it, especially the compact size and 4G compatibility with many phone companies in the US & abroad. Renewed items usually work without a problem. This phone can be recharged but it never recognizes a QC- or Turbo-charger and it takes a long time to get it to 100%. Using same cable & charger, other phone refill a lot faster. Battery life also isn't great but sufficient. Given the price of "only" $150, I keep it (grudgingly)
The battery does not last long. I bought the pixel 4a with 5G because of the battery was supposed to last. I use it for 3 hours and it's dead do not know why they promote long battery life.

Dead in months. The Pixel 4a was my first foray back into Android life after years being on the Apple train. It took some getting used to the navigation, but I managed pretty well. I liked the camera on the Pixel too - especially at night. BUT then I did the thing I’ve done a million times with my iPhone - I had it in my bag with a water bottle I didn’t screw the cap on tightly enough. The inside of the bag was a little wet and my phone had a message to not use the USB port until it dried up. Ok! Fine. A few hours later, my Pixel told me it was safe to use the port again, so I charged it that night as usual. Apparently that fried the battery - because the next day my phone couldn’t hold a charge, then couldn’t even turn on.

Turns off When Tapped (See Vid). [[VIDEOID:7d74711f636812d918b06d9d2ecbea40]] Just got the pixel 4a on Friday release day when all the Amazon units started arriving, 3 days ago and loved it. Battery life seemed great and the phone was snappy. But after the 2nd day I noticed the 4a would not stop rebooting and I could not figure it out as I was not running any new apps. After scratching my head and playing around with it, it seems to be a physical build quality issue where the battery power source is interrupted. See the video of me tapping the phone on my desk and it just turning off, repeatable every time. After I filmed this video the phone would not turn back on. I posted this issue to Reddit and someone else confirmed they had the exact same issue. There must be some major quality control issue.

I use my phone very frequently and usually charge it to 70 or 80% to preserve battery life. Even with all the usage, I usually only have to charge it once a day. It would definitely take a while to die with a full charge so no worries there. The thing I came across the most while researching the phone prior to purchasing was "it's a great budget phone" and I 100% agree. I'm no tech expert, but as a regular user, I can say this is the best phone I have ever had. In comparison with the Pixel 4 (which I do not have), the Pixel 4a does have a headphone jack, but does not have wireless charging or the squeeze feature, and is not water-resistant. I have the phone in "Just Black" and it is very nice and sleek with a white lock button.

Not very good. I have had the Google pixel 4a for almost a year now and I can safely say it's been one of the worse phones. Since the first week I got it, it was prone to overheat very quickly. Now recently I have had problems with it running out of battery in a little more than 2 hours. I have has 60 dollar androids that can handle heat bad last longer than this phone.

I usually don't have to worry about running out of juice and will often not plug it in before going to sleep. Many say the camera is getting long in the tooth (same sensor since Pixel 2) and that Google has extracted every bit of performance out of the old sensor with its computational photography and that an upgrade to a new sensor is needed to keep up with Apple and Samsung. That may be true, but in day-to-day, real world situations, it's plenty fine. Plus the fact they added an ultra-wide (nixing the 2x tele from Pixel 3 and 4) makes the camera more useful IN MY OPINION. Again, $500. Get the 4a 5G over the 5 unless you have to have waterproofing. It's $200 cheaper and 4a 5G even adds a headphone jack to boot.

Good phone, bad battery. My Pixel 4a 5G (renewed "Acceptable") arrived quickly and in very good cosmetic condition. However, the battery drains very quickly, and phone always feels warm even when not in use. I sent it back for a refund.

Charging port stopped working.. I bought a Pixel 4A in September of 2020. The charging port on my Pixel 4A stopped working. It won't accept charging male end of charging cord. It's a $100.00 repair bill.
